text:
alex: heads-up — saw a spike in 5xx after we flipped geo DNS weights to favor eu-west for latency steering, started ~1782449940 UTC.

marta: saw it too, dashboards lit up. spikes are mostly 502/504 from edge LBs serving model-infer proxies.

alex: packet captures show a lot of TCP resets from our egress NATs in eu-west-1a. suspected port exhaustion + backend health checks failing.

sam: could be ephemeral port reuse + aggressive health-check probing. did we change probe TTL/parallelism when we rolled the new failover policy?

marta: we did change probe policy last night — switched from single-region active probes to multi-region active probes with faster retries (200ms retry, 3 attempts) to detect regional degradations quicker.

alex: here's a small excerpt from the NAT logs:
```
2026-03-18T01:02:11Z nat-eu-1a kernel: conntrack: table full, dropping packet
2026-03-18T01:02:12Z nat-eu-1a app: ephemeral_ports_exhausted=1 reuse_rate=98% src=10.10.5.12
```

aditya: ugh — that explains it. when traffic shifted to eu-west due to geo steer, our reserved GPU clusters in eu-west started warming and created lots of short-lived outbound connections (model fetches, backend telemetry) which blew through NAT ports. cost hit is also visible — egress volume spiked and a lot went to premium cross-region links. rough estimate +$4.2k/day while it lasts.

sam: immediate mitigations: revert DNS weights (point back to us-west primary), scale nat gateways or move to NAT per-subnet, and throttle probe parallelism.

marta: agree. also change probe health check to reuse a persistent TCP connection to reduce port churn.

deploy-bot: rollout:geo-probe-policy v2 -> reverted (by marta) @ 1782450123 :thumbsup:

alex: rolling back weights now. will monitor 1m error rate.

ops-bot: alert suppressed for geo-dns-5xx-spike until 1782450900; annotation: "investigating NAT port exhaustion after geo weight change"

sam: medium-term: add connection pooling at model-proxy layer and enable source-NAT preservation (keepalive reuse), or put an egress gateway with 10x ephemeral ports. also consider using TCP port range expansion on our NAT instances.

aditya: longer-term cost/control idea: add region pinning config for heavy GPU workloads — route inference/model-warmup traffic to region where GPU capacity is reserved to avoid cross-region egress and unexpected cost. need RFC + config fields:
```
geo.routing:
  mode: latency
  heavy_workload_pin: true
  pin_rules:
    - tag: gpu-warmup
      preferred_region: eu-west-1
      fallback_policy: nearest_with_capacity
```

marta: also need safer fallback: when preferred region is unhealthy, fall back to a "same-cloud" region before cross-cloud. that reduces egress and keeps latency decent.

alex: action items we agreed: revert DNS weights (done), increase NAT capacity in eu-west for next 24h, change probe parallelism to 1 + increase probe interval to 5s, RFC for region-pin policy and per-AZ NAT gateways, and a follow-up cost analysis. I'll open a ticket.

sam: i'll put a small runbook in /runbooks/geo-failover for oncall: how to revert weights, increase NAT, and detect conntrack saturation.

marta: filing incident follow-up doc. the quick patch prevented more errors but we need a durable mitigation for port churn from model warmups.

aditya: ping me for the cost model, i'll run numbers for pinned vs unpinned egress.

alex: thanks all. marking this resolved for now; will post postmortem once we have telemetry. :white_check_mark:
